title: Fix XTRIM leaving a 0-live stream node that RDB cannot load
body:
Fix #15808

## Problem

`XTRIM` could leave a stream node with **no live entries**. RDB refuses to load that, so reload, replication, and persistence fail.

Example:

1. Add `1-0` and `2-0`, then `XDEL 2-0` (same node: one live entry, one tombstone).
2. `XTRIM MINID = 2-0` deletes `1-0` and stops at `2-0`.
3. The node is empty of live data, but it was not dropped — wholesale removal only ran when the node’s **last ID was below MINID**. A leftover tombstone at `2-0` blocked that, so the node stayed with **live = 0**.

RDB load checks each stream listpack’s live-entry count and treats `live <= 0` as corrupt (`"Stream listpack bad entry count"`). Empty nodes are not a valid encoding; they should be removed from the radix tree, not saved.

## Solution

If a trim pass deletes every live entry in a node, **remove the node**.

- Keep walking later nodes only when the whole node was already in the trim range.
- Otherwise stop — later IDs are past the trim bound.

Tests cover the tombstone + `XTRIM MINID` case: empty stream, no leftover radix-tree key, and `DEBUG RELOAD` still works.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes stream trim and in-memory structure cleanup on a persistence-sensitive path, though the behavior matches RDB’s expectations and is covered by a reload test.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Fixes `XTRIM` leaving radix-tree listpack nodes with zero live entries**, which RDB treats as corrupt and blocks reload/replication.
> 
> After per-entry trimming inside a node, the code now **drops the whole node whenever every live entry in that listpack was deleted** (`deleted_from_lp == entries`), instead of only doing so when the node already met the old “wholly past MINID/MAXLEN” removal criteria. That closes the gap where a **tombstone at the trim boundary** (e.g. `XDEL` then `XTRIM MINID`) could leave an empty-but-present node.
> 
> A new integration test asserts an empty stream, **no leftover radix-tree keys**, and a successful **`DEBUG RELOAD`**, with **`max-deleted-entry-id`** preserved.
>
